facts.f: The Sun is a star. It is the star closest to Earth.
facts.e: The Sun looks much bigger and brighter than other stars only because it is so much nearer to us.

facts.f: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
facts.e: The Sun is about 150 million km away, and light travels about 3 lakh km every second.

facts.f: There are eight planets in our Solar System.
facts.e: In order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

facts.f: Jupiter is the biggest planet in our Solar System.
facts.e: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

facts.f: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun.
facts.e: It races around the Sun once every 88 days.

facts.f: Venus is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
facts.e: Venus has a thick blanket of carbon dioxide that traps heat. Its surface is hot enough to melt lead.

facts.f: Mars is called the Red Planet.
facts.e: Its soil and rocks contain iron oxide, which is rust. Rust gives Mars its reddish colour.

facts.f: Saturn's beautiful rings are made mostly of chunks of ice and rock.
facts.e: The pieces range from tiny grains to boulders as big as houses.

facts.f: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.
facts.e: A satellite is something that travels around a planet. The Moon goes around Earth about once a month.

facts.f: We always see the same side of the Moon from Earth.
facts.e: The Moon takes the same time to spin once as it takes to go around Earth, so the same face always points at us.

facts.f: The Moon has no light of its own.
facts.e: Moonlight is sunlight bouncing off the Moon's surface towards us.

facts.f: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon, in July 1969.
facts.e: He landed with Buzz Aldrin on the Apollo 11 mission while Michael Collins circled above.

facts.f: Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union became the first human in space on 12 April 1961.
facts.e: His spacecraft, Vostok 1, went once around Earth in about 108 minutes.

facts.f: Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian to travel to space, in 1984.
facts.e: He flew aboard a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft and stayed on the Salyut 7 space station.

facts.f: India's Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023.
facts.e: India became the first country to land a spacecraft near the Moon's south polar region.

facts.f: India's Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit in 2014 on its very first try.
facts.e: The Mars Orbiter Mission made India the first Asian country to reach Mars orbit.

facts.f: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
facts.e: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once, but only about 225 Earth days to go around the Sun.

facts.f: Uranus spins tipped over on its side.
facts.e: Its axis is tilted by about 98 degrees, so it seems to roll around the Sun.

facts.f: Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun.
facts.e: It is so far away that one trip around the Sun takes about 165 Earth years.

facts.f: Pluto was called a dwarf planet in 2006.
facts.e: The International Astronomical Union decided Pluto is too small to clear its path around the Sun, so it is not counted as a full planet.

facts.f: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano known in the Solar System.
facts.e: It is more than twice as tall as Mount Everest.

facts.f: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm bigger than Earth.
facts.e: Astronomers have watched this storm swirl for more than 150 years.

facts.f: Our galaxy is called the Milky Way.
facts.e: It is a huge spiral of stars, gas and dust. Our Sun is just one of its billions of stars.

facts.f: A light-year measures distance, not time.
facts.e: It is how far light travels in one year: about 9.46 trillion km.

facts.f: After the Sun, the nearest star to Earth is Proxima Centauri.
facts.e: It is about 4.2 light-years away, so its light takes over four years to reach us.

facts.f: The Sun is made mostly of hydrogen and helium gas.
facts.e: Hydrogen is the most common, followed by helium. Only a tiny part is other elements.

facts.f: The Sun shines because of nuclear fusion.
facts.e: Deep inside the Sun, hydrogen nuclei join together to make helium and release huge amounts of energy.

facts.f: Stars twinkle because of Earth's air.
facts.e: Moving layers of air bend starlight a little this way and that, so the star seems to flicker.

facts.f: A black hole is a place where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.
facts.e: It forms when a huge amount of matter is squeezed into a very small space.

facts.f: Comets are balls of ice and dust. Near the Sun they grow glowing tails.
facts.e: A comet's tail always points away from the Sun, pushed by sunlight and the solar wind.

facts.f: A shooting star is not a star at all.
facts.e: It is a small bit of space rock burning up as it rushes into Earth's air. Scientists call it a meteor.

facts.f: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.
facts.e: It holds millions of rocky pieces left over from when the planets formed.

facts.f: The International Space Station goes around Earth about every 90 minutes.
facts.e: That means the astronauts on board see about 16 sunrises and sunsets every day.

facts.f: Astronauts float in the space station because they are falling around Earth.
facts.e: The station and everyone inside fall together around Earth all the time, so they feel weightless. Gravity is still there.

facts.f: Space is silent.
facts.e: Sound needs air, water or something solid to travel through. Space is almost empty, so sound cannot travel there.

facts.f: Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to go around the Sun.
facts.e: The extra quarter day adds up, so almost every four years we add 29 February. That is a leap year.

facts.f: The Moon's gravity causes most of the tides in Earth's oceans.
facts.e: The Moon pulls on the oceans, making the water bulge, so the sea rises and falls along the coast.

facts.f: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched in 1975.
facts.e: It was named after the great Indian mathematician and astronomer Aryabhata.

facts.f: Footprints on the Moon can last for a very long time.
facts.e: The Moon has no wind or rain to wipe them away.

facts.f: Saturn is so light for its size that it is less dense than water.
facts.e: It is made mostly of hydrogen and helium gas.

facts.f: Scientists estimate that the Universe is about 13.8 billion years old.
facts.e: They worked this out by studying light left over from the early Universe and how fast galaxies are moving apart.

facts.f: Earth is the only planet where life is known to exist.
facts.e: It has liquid water, air to breathe and just the right temperature.

facts.f: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth.
facts.e: The Moon blocks the Sun's light. In a lunar eclipse, Earth's shadow falls on the Moon instead.

facts.f: On Venus, the Sun rises in the west.
facts.e: Venus spins in the opposite direction to most planets.

facts.f: Kalpana Chawla was the first woman of Indian origin to go to space, in 1997.
facts.e: She flew on the American Space Shuttle Columbia as a mission specialist.

quiz.q: Which is the biggest planet in our Solar System?
quiz.x: Jupiter is so big that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

quiz.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
quiz.x: Mars has rusty, iron-rich soil that makes it look red.

quiz.q: Which planet is the hottest?
quiz.x: Venus's thick carbon dioxide air traps heat, so it is hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

quiz.q: Who was the first human to travel to space?
quiz.x: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth on 12 April 1961. Neil Armstrong was the first to walk on the Moon later, in 1969.

quiz.q: Who was the first Indian to travel to space?
quiz.x: Rakesh Sharma flew to space in 1984 on a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft.

quiz.q: How many planets are there in our Solar System?
quiz.x: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Pluto is a dwarf planet.

quiz.q: What is the name of our galaxy?
quiz.x: Our Sun is one of billions of stars in the Milky Way galaxy.

quiz.q: What does a light-year measure?
quiz.x: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion km.

quiz.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
quiz.x: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun.

quiz.q: Where is the asteroid belt?
quiz.x: Millions of rocky asteroids orbit the Sun between Mars and Jupiter.

quiz.q: What is a shooting star really?
o: A space rock burning up in Earth's air
quiz.x: Shooting stars are meteors: small space rocks that burn up high in the sky.

quiz.q: What is Pluto called today?
quiz.x: In 2006 astronomers decided Pluto is a dwarf planet.

quiz.q: Which Indian mission landed near the Moon's south pole in 2023?
quiz.x: Chandrayaan-3's lander Vikram touched down on 23 August 2023.

quiz.q: Which gas makes up most of the Sun?
quiz.x: The Sun is mostly hydrogen, with helium second.

quiz.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
quiz.x: Light covers the 150 million km from the Sun in about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

quiz.q: Which planet is famous for its bright, wide rings?
quiz.x: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock. Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune have faint rings too.

quiz.q: What causes most ocean tides on Earth?
quiz.x: The Moon's pull makes the ocean water bulge, so the sea level rises and falls.

quiz.q: What was India's first satellite called?
quiz.x: Aryabhata was launched in 1975. Bhaskara came later, in 1979.

quiz.q: Why does the Moon shine at night?
quiz.x: The Moon has no light of its own. It reflects light from the Sun.

quiz.q: Which is the farthest planet from the Sun?
quiz.x: Neptune is the eighth planet. Pluto is farther, but it is a dwarf planet.

quiz.q: On which planet is a day longer than its year?
quiz.x: Venus spins very slowly: one spin takes about 243 Earth days, but one orbit takes about 225.

quiz.q: Who was the first woman of Indian origin to go to space?
quiz.x: Kalpana Chawla flew on Space Shuttle Columbia in 1997.
